title: Count Good Nodes In Binary Tree
description: Count nodes whose value is at least every value on the path from the root to that node.
note: Pass the maximum value seen on the current path down each recursive branch.
notes: The problem guarantees a nonempty tree, so goodNodes takes TreeNode and starts with root.val as the path maximum. The helper takes TreeNode? because children can be absent; its none guard returns zero for an empty subtree.

Each recursive call has its own max_val parameter. Updating it for a node does not change the parent's parameter or the maximum used by a sibling branch. There is no captured accumulator or outer declaration.
Equality counts as good. Inside node.val >= max_val, assigning max_val = node.val already maintains the path maximum, so a separate max or max! operation is unnecessary.
dfs captures no state and is a separate function below goodNodes in both versions. Birdie registers function declarations before execution, so the main algorithm can call the helper written below it.
LeetCode supplies TreeNode. The record declaration shows how the same type would be defined in a standalone Birdie program.
The traversal takes O(n) time and O(h) recursion space, where h is the tree height. It does not modify the tree.
